message:
This PR implements cursor-based pagination alongside the existing offset-based pagination system, providing significant performance improvements for frequently updated datasets while maintaining full backward compatibility. ## Problem The current pagination system uses `OFFSET`/`LIMIT` queries which become inefficient for large datasets and can produce inconsistent results when data changes during pagination. For example, when moderators are reviewing reports that are being updated in real-time, traditional pagination can show duplicate items or skip entries as new reports are added. ## Solution The enhanced pagination system automatically detects and uses the most appropriate pagination method: - **Cursor-based pagination**: Uses indexed column values (like `id` or `updated_at`) for efficient navigation - **Offset-based pagination**: Continues to work for stable datasets like search results ### Key Features **🎯 Smart Mode Detection** ```html
``` **⚡ Performance Benefits** - Eliminates expensive `OFFSET` queries for large datasets - Provides consistent results when data changes during pagination - Uses efficient `WHERE id > cursor` conditions instead of `OFFSET` **🔧 Easy Integration** ```python # Backend: Generate cursors from data cursors = generate_pagination_cursors(reports, cursor_field='id', page_size=20) # Database: Efficient cursor-based queries async def find_reports_cursor(*, after=None, limit=20): query = SQL(""" SELECT * FROM report WHERE id > %s ORDER BY updated_at DESC, id DESC LIMIT %s """) ``` ## Implementation Details ### Backend (`app/lib/standard_pagination.py`) - Added `generate_pagination_cursors()` to create cursor values from datasets - Added `cursor_pagination_params()` to build efficient query parameters - Enhanced `ReportQuery` with cursor-based methods ### Frontend (`app/views/lib/standard-pagination.ts`) - Automatic detection of cursor vs offset pagination mode - Graceful fallback when cursors aren't available - Maintains existing API for seamless integration ### Database Queries - Uses indexed columns for efficient filtering (`WHERE id > cursor`) - Consistent ordering ensures predictable results - No changes required for existing offset-based queries ## Use Cases **✅ Ideal for Cursor-Based:** - Reports and moderation interfaces (implemented) - Audit logs and activity feeds - Comments and real-time data **✅ Ideal for Offset-Based:** - Search results and filtered lists - User directories - Static content archives ## Testing Comprehensive testing validates both pagination modes work correctly: ![Pagination Test Demo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f634c18b-1e4f-4d67-bae7-906a927cbec5) The screenshot shows both pagination modes functioning side-by-side: - **Top**: Cursor-based pagination displaying "Page 1 (100)", "Page 2 (90)" with cursor values - **Bottom**: Traditional pagination showing standard "Page 1", "Page 2" numbering ## Backward Compatibility Zero breaking changes - existing pagination continues to work unchanged. The system automatically uses cursors when available and falls back to traditional pagination otherwise. ## Documentation Complete implementation guide added in `CURSOR_PAGINATION.md` with examples for: - Backend query patterns - Frontend template usage - Controller implementation - Migration strategies This enhancement provides the foundation for efficient pagination across the platform while maintaining the simplicity and reliability of the existing system. --- 💡 You can make Copilot smarter by setting up custom instructions, customizing its development environment and configuring Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers.
